mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian Notary Public acting with the settlor and licensed resident agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of non-objection / name clearance certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, when submitted through a non-Hague-country consular office, Panamanian Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and proof of identity for settlor, foundation council members, protector (if any), and identified beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or embassy/consulate in the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing country is a Hague Convention member; otherwise Panamanian Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank and professional reference letters evidencing source of funds for the initial endowment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution or regulated professional firm in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Panamanian Consular Legalization for use in the AML/KYC file

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership declaration (Declaración de Titular Beneficiario) and entity ownership-chain chart
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Settlor through the licensed resident agent, filed with the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Government-only access filing; an apostilled certified copy may be prepared for international banking and counterparty due diligence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all settlors, foundation council members, protectors, beneficiaries, and any holder of powers of attorney against the OFAC SDN List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the national list maintained by Panama's Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF); enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including verification of beneficial ownership chain, source of wealth, and source of funds; the registered agent must retain screening evidence and file a written risk assessment before registration.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Portal de Servicios En Línea (Sede Electrónica de Trámites y Consultas)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed foundation name may be in Spanish or in any language using the Latin/Roman alphabet; non-Latin characters must be transliterated into Latin script; the name must be distinguishable from all existing registered entities in the Public Registry and must not contain misleading terms suggesting government sponsorship, banking, insurance, securities, or other regulated activities; all official charter documents submitted to the Public Registry must be in Spanish or accompanied by a certified Spanish translation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant or registered agent may file a motion for reconsideration before the Director General of the Registro Público within 5 business days of the refusal; if the motion is denied, an administrative appeal may be filed in accordance with the Public Registry’s internal procedures, followed by judicial review before the Third Administrative Chamber of the Supreme Court of Panama within two months; parallel filing of a replacement name is recommended to avoid transaction delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only as a commercial virtual-address arrangement supported by a licensed Panamanian resident agent maintaining a physical registered office in Panama; a fully virtual Private Interest Foundation with no resident agent or no Panamanian registered office is not permissible; foundation books and records may be kept or stored electronically outside Panama at the discretion of the foundation council.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a standard low-risk agri-commodity brokerage structure; quantified probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection in the first year is estimated below 5%, increasing to approximately 15% if trigger events arise such as PEP involvement, inconsistent UBO filings, adverse sanctions hits, or notification by a foreign financial intelligence unit.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law), as amended by Ley 46 de 2013 and Ley 70 de 2017; Arts. 1, 6, 15 and 22
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Sección de Personas Jurídicas, Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Fundación de Interés Privado (Notarized Foundation Charter and Bylaws)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the foundation endowment must be initially declared by the Founder. A practical minimum of USD 10,000 is recommended to satisfy third-party bank due diligence; funds are deposited at a Panama-regulated licensee or bank account, and no state escrow is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FORMAL FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION PA_PIF

RESOLVED, that the subscribers, acting as foundation councilors, adopt the Foundation Charter in accordance with Law No. 25 of 1995; approve the initial endowment and contributions made by the Founder; adopt the registered office at [address in Panama City]; and ratify the appointment of the following officers: Guardian/Owner of the Foundation, Resident Agent, and members of the Foundation Council. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Resident Agent be directed to complete the formalities before the Public Registry of Panama and that the Council preserve all records consistent with the statutory obligations. The chairperson, officers and councilors are each authorized to certify and execute any ancillary act. RESOLVED by unanimous consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Foundation Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Name Search Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal written name-search request to the Public Registry of Panama or through an authorized resident agent. Verify that the proposed foundation name is not confusingly similar to any registered corporate or foundation name. The reservation is valid for 30 days and may be renewed once.
required_dossiers: Written request signed by proposed councilor
Passport or incorporated body's corporate certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a revised name and pay the corresponding re-search fee; no formal appeal is needed unless the rejection is based on bad faith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Foundation Charter and Initial Endowment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the foundation charter containing the foundation's name, purposes, initial assets, council members, guardian and resident agent. Appear before a licensed Panamanian notary with the founder and the intended foundation councilors to execute the charter and any foundational bylaws. The notary will formalize the Escritura Pública and issue a protocol folio.
required_dossiers: Proof of initial endowment or asset transfer
Identification documents of founder and councilors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary observes defects, amend the charter and re-execute before the same notary; no court intervention is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration at the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Sección de Personas Jurídicas, Registro Público de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Escritura Pública with the Public Registry together with the corresponding registration fee and any required copies. The Registrar reviews the instrument for statutory compliance and issues a registered foundation certificate with a ficha folio.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registry fees
Consent and identification of Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a prevención or objection, cure the stated defect within the legal term by submitting a corrected amendment or supplemental notarial deed; appeal the final refusal before the Third Chamber of the Supreme Court as a last resort.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Legalization, Tax Registration and Banking
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and Municipality of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, obtain the foundation's RUC (tax identification) from DGI, complete the aviso de operación at the relevant Municipality, and open a corporate bank account with a Panama-regulated bank. Finalize the appointment of the foundation council and resident agent in the foundation minutes.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of councilors and Guardian
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality or DGI requests clarification, file the requested supporting documentation through the resident agent; if banking files are rejected, provide updated PEF and source-of-wealth declarations to the bank's compliance department.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable (pure brokerage and trading service).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: None required for pure office-based brokerage; if physical grain storage or handling is added, clearance must be obtained from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá and the Ministry of Health for operational premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - General Directorate of Revenue, Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF); official e-filing portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) File the Private Interest Foundation formation deed with the Public Registry of Panama and maintain a resident agent; 2) Inscribe the foundation in the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) via DGI Sede Electrónica, attaching the foundation deed, resident-agent certificate, and by-laws; 3) Activate the RUC and register for ITBMS, irrespective of active trading activity; 4) Obtain DGI pre-authorization for the electronic invoicing (SFEP) scheme at the Panamanian fiscal address. A PIF with exclusively foreign-source income receives a territorial-classification endorsement but remains obligated to file periodic nil or informative returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama applies a territorial-source income tax regime; no US-style check-the-box election exists, but the following statutory options are available: (a) election to be treated as a taxed entity on Panama-source income versus a passive foundation with nil liability; (b) election of the Pequeño Contribuyente small-taxpayer presumptive ITBMS regime where annual gross revenue does not exceed PAB 36,000; (c) voluntary ITBMS registration election to recover input credits during the export pre-shipment cycle; (d) written election to the DGI to zero-rate cross-border service export invoices under the Comprobante Fiscal Digital mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) - Panama's Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold: any person performing taxable transfers of goods or services in Panama must register for ITBMS before commencing activities. Simplified small-taxpayer threshold: PAB 36,000 annual gross taxable income.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing through the DGI Sistema de Facturación Electrónica de Panamá (SFEP). Invoices must be issued in XML/JSON and transmitted in real time to the DGI fiscal clearance platform (Sede Electrónica/API) to obtain a digital stamping authorization code; taxpayers must integrate ERP/billing systems via SFEP API web services; QR-code validation on the Comprobante Fiscal Digital is obligatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% ITBMS applies to: (a) export of goods physically shipped from Panama under a maritime export customs entry; (b) services rendered from Panama to non-residents 'effectively used or consumed abroad', including international brokerage of bulk agricultural commodities, whenever the beneficiary is abroad, payment originates from foreign funds, and no economic benefit arises within Panama. Supporting evidence must demonstrate receipt of foreign payment and foreign-based usage of the service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Aduanas / DUI) with port exit confirmation
Bill of Lading (B/L) for ocean transport of bulk grain parcels
Packing list and warehouse/silo delivery receipts
Inward remittance certificate: SWIFT MT103 or bank credit advice evidencing foreign payment
Charter-party or voyage contract identifying foreign principals / non-resident buyers
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI audits zero-rated export claims with high scrutiny on the transfer-pricing and fiscal nature of intra-group agri-brokerage commissions. Unsupported zero-rating gives rise to clawback of the 7% ITBMS plus a 10% surcharge, 1% monthly default interest, and fines up to PAB 10,000 under the Panama Fiscal Code; deliberate falsification of export documentation constitutes tax fraud punishable with imprisonment and prospective disqualification of the foundation's resident agent and legal counsel.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — Superintendency of Banks of Panama; Panama does not maintain a central bank, with the United States dollar serving as the circulating legal tender and monetary anchor.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full, unrestricted convertibility for both current and capital account transactions. The Panamanian balboa is pegged at par with the USD, and the USD itself is legal tender. There are no exchange-control authorisations, no licensing gates on profit remittance, and no repatriation tax or capital flight restrictions. Distributions, dividends, and beneficiary payments from a Private Interest Foundation are freely remittable after meeting routine AML/CFT record-keeping and banking verification requests.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation exists under Panamanian law. Exporters may retain all USD and other foreign currency receipts indefinitely and are not required to convert any percentage or observe a prescribed timeline for repatriation or monetisation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / Multipurpose Corporate Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium viability. Panama has no dedicated non-bank electronic-money institution (EMI) licensing regime; offshore EMIs cannot open a regulated settlement account or access the local clearing system without obtaining a banking licence from the SBP or operating through a licensed Panamanian bank as intermediary. Legal constraints include FATF-related enhanced due diligence expectations, a conservative custody over correspondent banking, and the requirement that any PAN PIF trade settlement flow pass through an SBP-regulated or equivalent high-tier foreign bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one Foundation Council member or an appointed authorised signatory is generally required for an in-person compliance interview at account opening. Remote opening may be permitted only for existing private-banking clients or with a strong banker-introduced relationship, provided that the Foundation deed, Public Registry good-standing certificate, certified passports, and all KYC source-of-wealth documents are apostilled and couriered to the bank. The interview is used to verify the ultimate beneficial owner, the commercial purpose of the bulk-grain brokerage, and the expected transaction profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF established with bearer participation certificates or undisclosed foreign beneficiaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Public Registry Certificate of the Foundation showing the Foundation Council, a sworn declaration of beneficiary designation, original deed with registered participation interests, certified passport copies, independent legal opinion from a Panamanian counsel, and notarised source-of-funds statement covering the initial endowment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border commodity brokerage payments involving counterparties from high-risk jurisdictions or unregulated exchanges.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully signed purchase and sale contracts, commercial invoices, bills of lading with vessel names, independent SGS/Bureau Veritas weight and quality certificates, payment-to-trade matching schedules, and proof that all counterparties maintain accounts at SBP-licensed or top-tier correspondent banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid fund velocity, thin initial capital, or interposed third-party funding inconsistent with the declared brokerage business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital escrow account statement evidencing the minimum endowment, bank-source questionnaire, six to twelve months of prior bank statements (if applicable), projected soybean and corn brokerage cash-flow model, and an executed AML/KYC policy showing adherence to Panama's Law 23 of 2015 and SBP Agreement 004-2023 KYC rules.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound USD injection is routed by SWIFT MT103 via a New York correspondent bank to the PIF's commercial bank trust account in Panama. The wire instruction must include the underlying purpose reference (e.g., 'PIF initial capital endowment' or 'ISIC 4631 bulk grain brokerage settlement pre-funding'); the remitter's bank must provide corresponding beneficial-owner and source-of-wealth evidence. No Panamanian exchange-control approval is required, but the receiving Panamanian bank will require a copy of the PIF deed, the commercial contract, and AML clearance before crediting the operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound grain-trade payments are cleared through SWIFT MT103/MT202 for direct disbursements and via irrevocable commercial letters of credit (MT700/MT707) when the counterparty is a Brazilian, Canadian, U.S., or European grain originator. All USD flows use the U.S. correspondent banking system (Fedwire/CHIPS) and are executed by the PIF's Panamanian bank under the reference 'ISIC 4631 bulk grain - soybean/corn purchase' together with the invoice and shipping summary. LC transactions must be issued in strict alignment with UCP 600 rules and require presentation of full title documents, bills of lading, and certificate of origin.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in COP, BRL, MXN and other controlled Latin American currencies
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (fixed-to-fixed or fixed-to-floating)
Vanilla FX options (USD/EUR and USD/JPY) on a principal basis
FX swaps for temporary liquidity repositioning between USD and foreign currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Government Renewal Fee (single annual franchise tax / tasa anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance; enforcement by Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before June 30 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues statutory penalty interest and administrative surcharges; the Public Registry will not issue good-standing certificates while the fee is outstanding; continued non-payment may lead to administrative suspension or strike-off of the foundation registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under Law 25 of 1995. Private Interest Foundations are not subject to a mandatory independent audit, and no revenue, asset, or size threshold triggers audit. Audit becomes required only if the foundation charter or Foundation Council expressly resolves to obtain an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No prescribed local GAAP for Private Interest Foundations; books must accurately reflect assets, liabilities, receipts, and disbursements and may be maintained under IFRS or generally accepted Panamanian accounting practice at the foundation's election.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual internal UBO confirmation is required: the registered agent must obtain a current signed beneficial ownership statement from the Foundation Council and retain it in the confidential UBO register. Any change in founder, Foundation Council member, beneficiary, protector, or controlling interest must be recorded and the UBO file updated within 30 days of the change. Share transfer confirmation is not applicable because a Private Interest Foundation has no share capital; analogous transfers of beneficial interests are evidenced by amended foundation records. Under Law 254 of 2021, the UBO register must be produced to Panamanian authorities upon lawful demand; failure to maintain or update the register exposes the foundation and its registered agent to monetary penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Foundation Council and Beneficiary Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutory; if voluntarily engaged, approximately US$2,500 – US$6,500 per audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial ISR; Panama-source income only; foreign-source income earned by a Panama Private Interest Foundation is outside the ISR base. Preferential rates apply only to exempt maritime/Colón Free Zone activities, not to inland grain brokerage; annual flat tax for PIF is B/.300–B/.350 instead of no tax? Need careful.
